title: Extreme Programming (XP): the technical practices of agile

videos.script: The agile manifesto promises to welcome change, even late. That promise is expensive. {{promise}} Change working code late, and something breaks that nobody notices for weeks. {{breaks}} Extreme Programming asks what a team has to do with its code to make that promise affordable. {{xp}} Its answer is a stack of feedback loops. A partner who reads every line as you type it. A test written before the code. Everybody's work merged several times a day. {{loops}} Each loop tells you that you are wrong as early as that mistake can be caught. {{early}} This lesson runs one test-first cycle for real, then looks at pairs, continuous integration, small releases and simple design. {{tour}} And it ends where XP and architects argue: which decisions can wait, and which cannot. {{argue}}
